headline: The requoter was ENABLED and RUNNING during the campaign. Its dominant refusal was NOTHING_TO_COMPLETE (163) -- there was no resting complement to reprice. Repricing cannot be the lever, because the order it would reprice was never placed.

deployment_verified.verifier: PASS false on 8 rows, all NO_APPROVAL_IN_FORCE -- correct for a disarmed service with no campaign approval

correction_1.what_I_claimed: L5_COMPLETION_REQUOTE is disabled by an unset variable, and that is 'the actual blocker'
correction_1.what_is_true: completion_requote_enabled reads TRUE in the running process, via the money path's own accessor
correction_1.how_I_got_it_wrong: I inferred it from the accessor default plus maybe_completion_requote showing 0.000s in L5_LIVE_TICK_STAGES. 0.000s meant FAST, not inert: halted and disarmed with zero open orders, there is no resting completion to requote, so it returns immediately.
correction_1.note: second time this session I inferred a switch state from absent telemetry and got it backwards; the first was L5_BOOK_COMPLETION. The row shipped in d29a4bf7 is what caught it.

correction_2.what_I_implied: the cancel-verification defect (7 verify_error + 3 still_open) was the key unlock for completions
correction_2.what_is_true: requote_refused:ORDERS_UNCERTAIN fired exactly ONCE in the campaign, and requote_cancelled succeeded once. e1758566 fixes a real defect, verified by 19 tests -- but it was not the dominant blocker of this campaign.
correction_2.status: e1758566 is deployed disarmed and remains worth having; its impact is smaller than I framed it

gate_isolation.source: L5_LIVE_HB counters, campaign deployment 134fba3a (SHA b8d2743c), read at 23:27:18 and 23:32:27 -- identical, so these are the settled campaign totals
gate_isolation.reading: NOTHING_TO_COMPLETE dominates at 163 of 184 refusals (88.6%). The requoter had no outstanding complement order to reprice.
gate_isolation.corroboration: independent and consistent with the earlier campaign audit: a complement was SUBMITTED in only 1 of the 4 windows (2245z). In the other three none was ever placed, so there was nothing to requote.
gate_isolation.attribution_caveat: the 163 is campaign-wide; I am attributing it to the three complement-less windows from the separate submission audit, not from a per-window counter. Two consistent sources, not one inference.

the_market_evidence.window_of_opportunity_s: <=16, at the fill tick, with 100,000 shares of depth

other_windows.2215z: only sub-0.96 moment is t+831s, past the 600s terminal, on a flash dislocation
other_windows.2300z: best 0.9800 at t+220s: under 0.99, never under 0.96

the_single_highest_impact_change.change: submit the INITIAL complement on the fill event, inside the fill tick, rather than waiting for the ingest-driven complement path.
the_single_highest_impact_change.why_this_and_not_repricing: 163 of 184 requote refusals are NOTHING_TO_COMPLETE. You cannot reprice an order that was never placed. The 0.99 cap, the requoter and the cancel-verify retry all operate downstream of a complement that does not exist.

the_timing_arithmetic.conclusion: the tick could reach it; the 18.11s ingest median lands at t+148, exactly at the crossing

the_single_highest_impact_change.what_is_NOT_yet_established: WHY the initial complement was not submitted in those three windows. The submission audit says it was not; the requote counters say there was nothing to reprice. Neither says which gate refused the initial submission at t+130. That is the next question, and it is a different gate from everything examined so far.
the_single_highest_impact_change.explicitly_not_proposed: no code change is proposed in this artifact. Three times in this session I have inferred a mechanism from indirect evidence and been wrong twice; the initial-submission gate will be named from telemetry before anything is written.
